question: An operations analyst is comparing eight vendors and must decide whether to ask Claude for prose or for a structured table with fixed columns. Which two are sound reasons to choose the structured form? Select two.
options: A) The results will be moved into a tracker where every field has to line up exactly.
B) Tables remove the need to check the content, because the figures are already aligned.
C) Structured output is inherently more accurate than the same content written as prose.
D) A fixed set of columns makes it obvious when a vendor has no value for a field.
E) Producing a table takes Claude noticeably less effort than writing flowing paragraphs.
correct_answers: A) The results will be moved into a tracker where every field has to line up exactly.
D) A fixed set of columns makes it obvious when a vendor has no value for a field.
explanations: Correct. When output feeds a downstream system, a predictable field structure removes the manual re-keying that prose would force the analyst to do by hand.
Alignment is presentational. A neat table still needs the same accuracy and completeness checks as any other output before it is relied on.
Format does not change correctness. A table can hold exactly the same wrong figure as a paragraph, presented rather more convincingly.
Correct. Visible gaps are a curation benefit distinct from downstream use: prose can pass over a missing vendor detail without the omission ever showing.
Relative effort is not a reason a knowledge worker should choose a format. The decision should follow from how the information will be used.
